To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adult MSCs have trophic effects on the repair of injured tissue.
MSCs are a source of trophic mediates that are beneficial in the repair of tissue damaged by infarction, stroke or meniscus injury.

1) MSCs have the potential to secrete trophic factors that can enhance the reparative process in damaged tissue; 2) the MSC secretome is a complex mixture that is influenced by the tissue microenvironment; 3) MSC trophic activity is influenced by the type of injury and by the tissue type; and 4) MSC trophicity is not limited to a single tissue type and can be used to enhance repair in several tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of stem cells in the treatment of disease, particularly in the area of regenerative medicine and tissue engineering
the use of MSC to treat a number of diseases and disorders, including: 1) heart attack, 2) stroke, 3) osteoarthritis, and 4) diabetes.
the use of MSC for the repair of damaged tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MSCs have a variety of trophic effects that may be beneficial in tissue repair.

MSCs are a very promising cell therapy for the treatment of a variety of degenerative diseases, but further research is needed to determine the optimal dose and route of administration, the best source of MSCs (bone marrow, adipose tissue, umbilical cord blood, or other), and the best method of expansion and differentiation of MSCs.
the trophic effects of MSCs in vivo are real, but the mechanisms by which they occur are not yet understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MSCs are a promising cell source for tissue repair.
the use of mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) in tissue repair models is an attractive strategy for enhancing the reparative process.

we have shown that the MSCs have a very powerful trophic effect in the heart, and that they can be used in the treatment of acute MI, chronic ischemic heart disease, and in the setting of heart failure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MSCs are not a single type of cell but a collection of cells with diverse phenotypes and functions.
the paracrine effects of MSCs are important in tissue repair, and that the paracrinemediated effects are distinct from the differentiation of MSCs to tissue repair cells.
the use of adult marrow derived mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) transplantation for the treatment of tissue injury or disease is not limited to their direct differentiation into repair tissue.
